_doc: Manual mapping from the 80 class labels (models/classes.json) to a representative Wikipedia article and taxon. 'taxon' is the name queried on iNaturalist (and GBIF unless 'gbif_name' is given; gbif_name null = no GBIF key). 'is_group' = the label is a group of species, not one species; groups, domestic forms and hybrids never get a species-level IUCN status. Optional pins: inat_taxon_id, gbif_taxon_key, image_file (Commons file name).

Bear.rank_note: group — represents family Ursidae (all eight bear species)

Bull.rank_note: domestic — an adult male of domestic cattle (Bos taurus); taxon data is for Bos taurus

Butterfly.rank_note: group — represents butterflies, superfamily Papilionoidea (order Lepidoptera)
Butterfly.gbif_note: GBIF backbone has no superfamily rank; map uses order Lepidoptera (includes moths)

Camel.rank_note: group — represents genus Camelus (dromedary, Bactrian camel, wild Bactrian camel)

Canary.rank_note: domestic — the domestic canary, a domesticated form of the Atlantic canary (Serinus canaria); taxon data is for the wild species

Caterpillar.rank_note: group — a larval stage, not a taxon; represents larvae of order Lepidoptera (butterflies and moths)

Chicken.rank_note: domestic — domestic chicken, a domesticated subspecies of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus)

Crab.rank_note: group — represents true crabs, infraorder Brachyura

Duck.rank_note: group — ducks are an informal (paraphyletic) group within family Anatidae, which also contains geese and swans

Eagle.rank_note: group — eagles are an informal group of large raptors within family Accipitridae (not a single clade)

Elephant.rank_note: group — represents family Elephantidae (African bush, African forest and Asian elephants)

Fish.rank_note: group — 'fish' is not a natural taxon; represented here by ray-finned fishes (Actinopterygii), which make up ~99% of fish species
Fish.gbif_note: Actinopterygii is not a rank in the current GBIF backbone; no GBIF key

Fox.rank_note: group — represents true foxes, genus Vulpes (several other canid genera are also called foxes)

Frog.rank_note: group — represents order Anura (frogs and toads)

Giraffe.rank_note: species — IUCN assesses giraffes as one species, Giraffa camelopardalis (some authorities split it into four)

Goldfish.rank_note: domestic — the goldfish is a domesticated fish; taxon data is for Carassius auratus, which also has wild populations

Goose.rank_note: group — true geese (genera Anser and Branta, tribe Anserini); data uses genus Anser (grey geese)

Hamster.gbif_note: GBIF backbone has no subfamily rank; map uses family Cricetidae (includes voles and New World mice)

Hedgehog.gbif_note: GBIF backbone has no subfamily rank; map uses family Erinaceidae (includes gymnures)

Hippopotamus.rank_note: species — the common hippopotamus (the pygmy hippo is a separate genus)

Horse.rank_note: domestic — domestic horse (Equus ferus caballus / Equus caballus)

Jellyfish.rank_note: group — 'jellyfish' covers medusae of several cnidarian classes; represented by class Scyphozoa (true jellyfish)

Kangaroo.rank_note: group — kangaroos are the largest members of family Macropodidae (genera Macropus and Osphranter); data uses the whole family

Ladybug.rank_note: group — represents family Coccinellidae (ladybirds / lady beetles)

Lizard.rank_note: group — lizards are a paraphyletic group of squamates; iNaturalist groups them as suborder Sauria
Lizard.gbif_note: GBIF backbone has no lizard taxon; map uses Squamata (includes snakes)

Magpie.rank_note: group — 'magpie' covers several corvid genera; represented by genus Pica (incl. the Eurasian magpie)

Monkey.rank_note: group — monkeys are a paraphyletic group (Simiiformes excluding apes); data uses infraorder Simiiformes, which includes apes
Monkey.gbif_note: GBIF backbone has no infraorder rank; map uses order Primates

Mouse.rank_note: group — 'mouse' covers many small rodents; represented by genus Mus (incl. the house mouse)

Mule.rank_note: hybrid — offspring of a male donkey and a female horse; not a species
Mule.gbif_note: hybrids have no GBIF backbone key

Ostrich.rank_note: species — the common ostrich (the Somali ostrich is a separate species)

Otter.gbif_note: GBIF backbone has no subfamily rank; map uses family Mustelidae (includes weasels, badgers)

Panda.rank_note: species — mapped to the giant panda (the red panda is a separate class label)

Pig.rank_note: domestic — domestic pig, a domesticated form of the wild boar (Sus scrofa)

Rabbit.rank_note: group — rabbits are the non-hare members of family Leporidae; data uses the whole family (incl. hares)

Raven.rank_note: species — 'raven' is used for several Corvus species; mapped to the common raven, the most widespread

Rhinoceros.rank_note: group — represents family Rhinocerotidae (five living species)

Sea lion.rank_note: group — sea lions are part of family Otariidae (eared seals, which also includes fur seals)

Sea turtle.rank_note: group — represents superfamily Chelonioidea (seven living species)
Sea turtle.gbif_note: GBIF backbone has no superfamily rank; map uses family Cheloniidae (all sea turtles except the leatherback)

Shark.rank_note: group — represents sharks (Selachimorpha; iNaturalist infraclass Selachii)
Shark.gbif_note: GBIF backbone has no shark-only taxon; map uses class Elasmobranchii (includes rays)

Shrimp.rank_note: group — 'shrimp' is not a single taxon; represented by caridean shrimp (infraorder Caridea)
Shrimp.gbif_note: GBIF backbone has no infraorder rank; map uses order Decapoda (includes crabs, lobsters)

Snail.rank_note: group — 'snail' covers shelled members of class Gastropoda

Sparrow.rank_note: group — represents Old World sparrows, family Passeridae (American sparrows are a separate family)

Squid.rank_note: group — represents superorder Decapodiformes (squid and cuttlefish relatives)
Squid.gbif_note: GBIF backbone has no Decapodiformes/Teuthida taxon; map uses class Cephalopoda (includes octopuses, cuttlefish, nautiluses)

Turkey.rank_note: species — the wild turkey, Meleagris gallopavo; the domestic turkey is a domesticated form of the same species

Turtle.rank_note: group — represents order Testudines (all turtles and tortoises)

Whale.rank_note: group — 'whale' is informal; represented by Cetacea (which also includes dolphins and porpoises)

Worm.rank_note: group — 'worm' is not a taxon; represented by earthworms (order Crassiclitellata, phylum Annelida)

Zebra.rank_note: group — three zebra species (subgenus Hippotigris of Equus); map and observations use the plains zebra (Equus quagga) as the representative species
